title: Decoupling: what it is, what it costs

lines.say: You and your spouse own a condo together. Buying a second home means 20% extra stamp duty.
lines.cap: a second home means *20% extra* stamp duty

lines.say: Some couples look at decoupling: one spouse sells their share to the other.
The one who's out may then buy as a first time buyer, without that 20%.
lines.cap: then buy as a *first time buyer*

lines.say: But it isn't free. Buyer's stamp duty is due on the share transferred, plus legal fees.
lines.cap: *not free*: stamp duty on the share, plus legal fees

lines.say: CPF used for that share goes back to CPF, and the remaining owner may need a new loan.
Sometimes the costs outweigh the savings. Get legal advice before you start.

caption:
Own a condo with your spouse and thinking of a second home? That usually means 20% ABSD. 🏢

Some couples look at decoupling: one spouse sells their share to the other, so the one who's out may buy as a first time buyer.

But it isn't free: buyer's stamp duty on the share transferred, legal fees, CPF refunded with interest, and the remaining owner may need a new loan. Sometimes the costs outweigh the savings. Get legal advice before you start.
